leads.reason: Access uncertain. Reverse-geocodes to the Rue de Tunis / Minimes area, near amenity=bench and leisure=picnic_table OSM features (suggesting a park setting), but local reporting found this pass describes a specific green space on Rue de Tunis, the Jardin des Capucins, as currently PRIVATELY owned by the housing company Promologis, with residents campaigning to have it made public. This candidate and its two neighbours (128440, 128428) may or may not sit inside that private plot; not resolved this pass. Coordinates: 43.6190, 1.4453.

leads.name: Photinia x fraseri 'Red Robin', near Basilique Saint-Sernin
leads.reason: Qualification uncertain rather than access: located at a genuinely public, prominent site (next to the Basilique Saint-Sernin, a UNESCO World Heritage church), but Photinia x fraseri 'Red Robin' is a modern (1940s Australia/New Zealand) ornamental cultivar normally grown as a hedge or small shrub for its red new leaves, not a species typically capable of being genuinely old or visually spectacular as an individual specimen. Worth a photo check before shipping: if this individual has been grown to unusual tree form or size, it could qualify, but the register alone does not establish that. Coordinates: 43.6087, 1.4423.

NOTE: this is NOT the famous bald cypress in a pond at Jardin des Plantes described by France3 Regions' 2025 survey (planted ~150 years ago, aerial roots visible in a garden basin) - that tree's real coordinates do not match this candidate, and no register entry in this pass's 29-tree set corresponds to it. That Jardin des Plantes cypress is a genuine gap worth importing/researching separately in a future pass. This Mirail candidate itself reverse-geocodes to a playground area, plausibly public but unresearched and far from the main cluster.
